notes.meaning: Wine and strong drink are pictured as people: one mocks and the other picks fights. They make a fool of the drinker. They promise good feelings but end up biting. A person who lets drink lead him astray shows he is not wise, and he makes it harder to become wise.

An angry king is as frightening as a roaring lion. Whoever stirs up his anger puts his own life in danger. If it is foolish to anger an earthly king, it is far more foolish to anger God, the King of kings.

People often think backing down from a fight is shameful, but it is really honorable. A wise person stays out of quarrels, or drops them, even giving up what he has a right to for the sake of peace. Abraham did this with Lot. Only a fool is always ready to start a fight.

The lazy man finds an excuse, like cold weather, not to plow when it is time. So when harvest comes, he looks for a crop and finds nothing. The same is true of our souls: small troubles should not keep us from what matters most.

What a person plans in his heart is hidden, like water at the bottom of a deep well. A person with good sense can still draw it out, often by asking wise questions. This also works with quiet, wise people who have much good advice but do not speak up unless asked.

Many people talk about how kind and generous they are. But a truly faithful person, who does more good than he talks about and stays true in hard times, is rare. Kindness is easy to find. Faithfulness is not.

A good person lives with honesty and a clear conscience. He does not have to worry about lies catching up with him. His children are blessed because of him, through God's promises and his good example. That blessing starts even while he is alive.

This describes a good king, not every king. When he sits to judge and looks into matters himself, wrongdoers cannot stand before him, and evil is scattered. When powerful people are also good people, they can do much good and stop much evil.

The answer to this question is "no one." No person in this life can honestly say his heart is fully clean of sin. Even good people still struggle with sin inside. By God's grace (His kindness we do not earn) we may be cleaner than we were, but that is the Holy Spirit's work, not our own.

differ.view: No one can make his own heart clean, but many believers can truly say the blood of Jesus has cleansed them from all unrighteousness.

notes.meaning: In those days goods were weighed on scales with stone weights. A cheater kept two sets: a heavy one for buying and a light one for selling. God hates this and every kind of cheating in business. He will not bless what is gained this way.

Even a young child shows what he is like by what he does. Children have not yet learned to hide who they are. Parents should watch their children closely so they can guide them well, and even notice what kind of work they may be suited for.

God made our ears and eyes, so all our abilities come from Him and should be used for Him. Since God made the eye and ear, He surely sees and hears all we do. He also gives the inner ear and eye that hear His voice and see His goodness.
Our bodies need sleep, but we should not love it for its own sake. Too much sleep makes a person careless and leads to poverty. Wake up, get to work, and you will have enough to eat.

A buyer runs down the goods to get a low price: "It's no good!" Then he walks off and brags about the great deal he got. This is a kind of lying, and a person should be ashamed of it, no matter how much he saves.

Gold and jewels are easy to find compared with wise words. Lips that speak true knowledge are a rare and precious treasure, worth more than riches. If we really believed this, we would value God's word as it deserves.

"Posting security" means promising to pay someone else's debt if they fail. A person who does this carelessly for strangers is heading for ruin. So if you lend to him, take something of his, even his coat, as a guarantee. Hard as that sounds, it may teach him not to be so rash.

What is gained by cheating can taste sweet at first, because it came easily. But later it is like a mouth full of gravel. Sin may be pleasant for a moment, but it turns bitter when the conscience wakes up.

Good plans come from careful thought and good advice, and most of all from asking God for direction. Hasty choices are often regretted. This is especially true of something as serious as war, which should never be started without wise counsel.

A gossip goes around telling secrets. Do not get close to someone who cannot keep his mouth shut. If he tells you others' secrets, he will tell yours too. Be careful also of flatterers, who often use sweet talk to get stories out of you.

God's law treated cursing your father or mother as a very serious crime. Such a person's "lamp," meaning his life, honor, and future family, will go out in deep darkness. It is the opposite of the promise in the command to honor your parents.
Wealth grabbed too quickly, by dishonest means or even by a child seizing his parents' property early, will not be blessed. What rises fast often falls fast, because God's blessing is not on it.

When someone wrongs you, do not plan to get even, not even in your heart. Trust the matter to God and wait for Him. Notice that God does not promise to punish your enemy, but to help and protect you, and that is enough. Meanwhile, pray for the one who hurt you.

This repeats the warning about cheating weights, because God hates it so much and it was common then. The added words say it is "no good" even for the cheater. A deal won by fraud turns out to be a losing deal in the end.
We depend on God for every step we take. We make choices and are responsible for them, but God guides how things work out. We cannot see the whole path ahead, so we should trust our way to Him.

It is a trap to quickly promise something to God and then later look for ways out of the promise. Think carefully before you make a vow (a solemn promise to God), not after. It is also wrong to take for yourself what has been given to God.

Farmers ran a heavy wheel over grain to separate it from the husks. In the same way, a wise ruler separates out wicked people and gives them the punishment they deserve. Firm justice protects everyone else.

God has put a lamp inside every person: our mind and conscience. Like a light carried through a dark house, it searches our hidden thoughts and motives. We should use it to test our hearts by what God has said.

A king is kept safe by steady love and faithfulness. Love is mentioned twice, so it should be at the center of how he rules. Mercy and truth are the glory of God's own throne, and they make a ruler loved and secure.

Young people shine with strength. Older people shine with gray hair, a sign of wisdom and experience. Each age has its own gift, so the young and the old should neither look down on nor envy each other.

Hard correction can clean out evil, the way cleaning a wound helps it heal. Strict discipline can reach deep into the heart and turn a person from wrong. God sometimes uses hard times the same way for His children, and that is a reason to be thankful.
